translation: As for the wei-qi, it issues out the keen and swift nature of its hasty (han) qi, and first [runs] among the four extremities and the divisions of flesh and skin, without rest: by day it travels in the yang and by night it travels in the yin, constantly from the division of Foot Shaoyin, traveling through the five zang and six fu. Now, when rebellious qi (jueqi) lodges in the five zang and six fu, then the wei-qi alone guards its exterior, traveling in the yang yet unable to enter the yin; traveling in the yang then the yang-qi is exuberant, with the yang-qi exuberant the Yang Qiao sinks (xian); and being unable to enter the yin then the yin-qi is deficient, and therefore the eyes do not close.
